author: lifewithoutlana
text: Everyone is talking about Macy’s removing its famous red shopping bag sign. ⏎  ⏎ But the real story is the tiny building hidden behind it for more than a century. ⏎  ⏎ When Macy’s planned its Herald Square flagship in the early 1900s, it began assembling the properties needed for the enormous store. It bought nearly everything on the site, except a small corner parcel at 34th Street and Sixth Avenue. ⏎  ⏎ The lot measured only about 30 by 50 feet, but it controlled one of the most important corners in Herald Square. ⏎  ⏎ The property was reportedly owned by Reverend Duane Pell, who understood exactly how much leverage that location gave him. Historical accounts say he wanted approximately $250,000, an extraordinary amount for such a small piece of land at the time. ⏎  ⏎ Macy’s eventually appears to have been willing to buy it. ⏎  ⏎ But before the deal could be completed, Pell sold the parcel for approximately $375,000 to an agent connected to Henry Siegel, the owner of Macy’s rival, Siegel-Cooper. ⏎  ⏎ Siegel then reportedly offered Macy’s the corner in exchange for one of Macy’s former 14th Street properties. ⏎  ⏎ Macy’s refused. ⏎  ⏎ Instead, Macy’s built its new flagship around the parcel, leaving the small building embedded in the corner of one of the largest department stores in the world. ⏎  ⏎ The rival store eventually lost control of the property, and Macy’s later leased the building’s exterior for advertising. For decades, the structure was hidden behind enormous billboards, including the iconic red shopping bag sign millions of New Yorkers recognize. ⏎  ⏎ Now that the billboard is being dismantled, the old five-story holdout building is visible again. ⏎  ⏎ This story shows that value is not always about size. ⏎  ⏎ A tiny parcel can have enormous power when it controls the right corner, interrupts a land assembly, or becomes essential to someone else’s development plan. ⏎  ⏎ In Manhattan real estate, the most valuable property is sometimes not the biggest one. ⏎  ⏎ It is the one somebody else desperately needs. ⏎  ⏎ Follow for more real estate knowledge ❤️

author: kenishshah_14
text: The beauty of a company takeover transaction? You can buy the asset without actually buying the asset. 👀 ⏎  ⏎ I recently sold a ₹34 Cr commercial property in Andheri West — but the buyer didn’t actually buy the property. ⏎  ⏎ Instead, they bought 100% of the shares of the company that owned it. ⏎  ⏎ The property stayed exactly where it was. ⏎ Only the ownership of the company changed. ⏎  ⏎ And because it was structured as a share sale instead of a traditional property sale, the buyer avoided the usual stamp duty, registration and transfer charges — saving almost ₹3 Cr. ⏎  ⏎ But here’s the catch 👇 ⏎  ⏎ When you buy the company, you also inherit its history. ⏎  ⏎ Loans. Litigation. ROC filings. Contracts. Liabilities. Tax implications. Everything. ⏎  ⏎ That’s why a company takeover isn’t simply a “hack” to save stamp duty. It’s a structuring strategy that needs proper legal and tax due diligence. ⏎  ⏎ And this is the bigger lesson: ⏎  ⏎ Smart real estate investors don’t just think about how they’ll buy an asset. They think about how they’ll hold it — and eventually exit it. ⏎  ⏎ A clean SPV. A single asset. A well-structured transaction. ⏎  ⏎ That can make a massive difference when it’s time to sell. ⏎  ⏎ Everyone knows how to buy property. The smarter investors think about how to structure the ownership. ⏎  ⏎ In no way is this financial advice to avoid paying any charges, please consult your CA and lawyer to check if this structure works for you! ⏎  ⏎ Follow me if you want to see more real commercial real estate deals, numbers and structures from the Mumbai market. ⏎  ⏎ #CommercialRealEstate #RealEstateInvesting #MumbaiRealEstate #CommercialProperty #RealEstateIndia

author: e_brody
text: Your $50M development just became a $55M development. ⏎  ⏎ Congratulations. Now go find another $5 million. ⏎  ⏎ Construction costs rise. Schedules extend. Interest carry increases. But your lender doesn’t automatically increase proceeds because your budget changed. ⏎  ⏎ That extra capital has to come from somewhere: more sponsor equity, additional LP equity, pref, mezz, a capital call—or a complete rethink of the deal. ⏎  ⏎ That’s why a development budget isn’t just a construction document. It’s a capital markets document. ⏎  ⏎ Change the cost of the building → you change the debt structure → you change the equity requirement → you change the returns. ⏎  ⏎ And if your deal only works because you’re still using a construction budget from 12 months ago, you don’t have a development plan. ⏎  ⏎ You have a very expensive imagination. ⏎  ⏎ #CommercialRealEstate #RealEstateDevelopment #CapitalMarkets #CRE #ANAX

text: I Visited 4 Massive Vintage Warehouses in Normandy, France (Full Price Reveals!) || Exploring vintage warehouses near Rouen 📍 Get the Paris Vintage Sourcing Kit: https://maisonamaranth.com/products/z... ⏎  ⏎ 💌 Shop our antique collection: https://maisonamaranth.com/collection... ⏎ 🗺️ Get the Vintage Master Map (400+ locations): https://maisonamaranth.com/products/t... ⏎ 🧺 Get your 2026 Fair Calendar: https://maisonamaranth.com/products/t... ⏎  ⏎ In today's video, join me (Indra, founder of Maison Amaranth) as we leave central Paris behind and head deep into the Normandy countryside around Rouen to explore four completely different types of giant clearance and thrift depots. If you love the French country aesthetic but want to skip the high-end retail markups of the city, these regional warehouses are where the actual deals are hiding. ⏎  ⏎ From 19th-century Belle Époque armoires and French faience tureens to a matching set of mid-century oak dining chairs, we are breaking down real prices, transport logistics, and the ultimate sourcing rules. ⏎  ⏎ In this Normandy thrift warehouse sourcing vlog, we are covering: ⏎ 1. Happy Troc (Barentin): A massive commercial consignment warehouse packed with regional furniture, vintage ceramics, and an incredible set of oak ladder-back chairs. ⏎ 2. Le Dépôt du Meuble (Croixmare): A sprawling rural furniture depot housing large-scale statement pieces, rustic tables, and stunning double-door mirrored armoires. ⏎ 3. Au Vide Grenier (Notre-Dame-de-Bondeville): An indoor permanent flea market on the northern edge of Rouen featuring curated vendor booths full of smalls and decor. ⏎ 4. Ressourcerie Résistes (Darnétal): A non-profit eco-center east of Rouen offering hidden treasure troves of pre-loved homeware and books. ⏎  ⏎ Thrift Warehouse Sourcing & Navigation Tips ⏎ Entrance & Logistics Opening Hours: Vary by location (typically open Wednesday through Saturday, with select afternoon hours). Check individual store schedules before making the drive! ⏎ Getting There: Renting a car is essential.
